title: Hoax Bomb Threats Disrupt At Least 25 Flights Across Europe
dek: Threats hit Ryanair, Aer Lingus, easyJet and other carriers for the second time this week. Police say the Heathrow threats were hoaxes, and investigators have found no evidence of a state or terror group behind them.
author: Meridian Newsroom
keyPoints: The Guardian reported at least 25 flights across Europe were disrupted Thursday by hoax bomb threats, with some forced into emergency landings. CNBC reported dozens of flights were affected.

Airlines named by the Guardian include Ryanair, Aer Lingus, Wizz Air, Finnair, easyJet, Aegean Airlines, Iberia and LOT Polish Airlines. All landed safely, and searches of the planes found nothing suspicious.
The Metropolitan Police said threats against four aircraft at or bound for Heathrow were hoaxes, and that "no security issues [were] identified" after an assessment.

The Guardian reported at least 33 flights have been affected this week. Investigators said there was no evidence so far that a hostile terror group or state actor, such as Russia or Iran, was behind the threats.
body:
Hoax bomb threats forced planes to divert, land early or be searched at airports across Europe on Thursday, the second day of such incidents this week, according to the Guardian and CNBC.

## What happened

The Guardian reported that at least 25 flights were disrupted, with some forced into emergency landings. Two Ryanair flights from Copenhagen and Madrid made emergency landings in Sofia, Bulgaria, according to the Guardian. The affected routes spanned Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia and Czechia. All flights landed safely, and searches found nothing suspicious, the Guardian reported. CNN said the diversions came two days after at least seven flights received similar threats.

The Guardian also reported that a Ryanair flight from Pescara, Italy, to Brussels-Charleroi was inspected after the word “bomb” was found written in its onboard toilet. A Cork airport spokesperson confirmed to the Guardian that an anonymous phone threat caused a flight to be delayed on Thursday morning.

## UK response

The Metropolitan Police said threats had been made against four aircraft departing from or arriving at Heathrow, and that Heathrow and Birmingham airports received threats overnight. After assessment by specialist investigators from the force’s aviation police command, the threats were determined to be hoaxes. The force said “no security issues [were] identified.”

## Emails and investigation

Bomb threats emailed to airports in Rome and Sofia were signed “fighters of the Male State,” according to sources at Aeroporti di Roma and a text seen by AFP, the Guardian reported. The Guardian described Male State as a Russian far-right movement; its founder did not comment on or claim responsibility for the threats, the paper reported. Investigators said Thursday there was no evidence so far that a hostile terror group or state actor, such as Russia or Iran, was behind the hoaxes. Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto told reporters the campaign was “under-threshold warfare” below the attribution threshold. The Kremlin called blame for the threats “absurd,” according to the Guardian.

## Scale and industry response

The Guardian reported at least 33 flights have been affected this week. It said the Thursday disruptions were a tiny fraction of the 27,400 flights scheduled in Europe that day, according to Eurocontrol. IATA condemned the disruption and urged authorities to identify the origin of the threats. EU transport commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas said it was too early to know if the incidents were linked. Meridian will update this story if investigators identify a source or if further threats are reported.
